# Configuration

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_config_docs.py from python/fbfast/_native.pyi; do not edit. -->

`FirebirdConfig()` resolves every option from, in order: the explicit keyword
argument, the `FB_<NAME>` environment variable, the same variable in a `.env`
file in the current directory, and the default below. `database`, `user` and
`password` are required. Construction validates all values and never connects.

```python
import fbfast

config = fbfast.FirebirdConfig()                      # FB_* variables and .env
config = fbfast.FirebirdConfig(pool_size=4, query_timeout=10.0, env_file=False)
config = fbfast.FirebirdConfig.from_env("FB_BI_")     # FB_BI_HOST, FB_BI_DATABASE...
```

In the environment and `.env`, numbers are text, booleans accept
`true/false`, `1/0` and `yes/no`, and `none` means `None`. Durations are
seconds. An explicit `None` wins over the environment for options that accept
it. Unknown options and invalid values raise `ConfigurationError`.

| Option | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | `FB_HOST` | `"localhost"` | Firebird server host name or address (non-empty str). |
| `port` | `FB_PORT` | `3050` | TCP port (int, 1..65535). |
| `database` | `FB_DATABASE` | `required` | Database alias or path on the server (non-empty str). |
| `user` | `FB_USER` | `required` | Firebird user (non-empty str). |
| `password` | `FB_PASSWORD` | `required` | Password (non-empty str), hidden in repr. Accessing config.password returns a normal str; never log it. |
| `role` | `FB_ROLE` | `None` | SQL role to activate (str \| None). An explicit None ignores a role from the environment. |
| `read_only` | `FB_READ_ONLY` | `True` | Only True is supported (Literal[True]); False raises UnsupportedFeatureError. |
| `charset` | `FB_CHARSET` | `"UTF8"` | Connection charset (non-empty str). Only UTF8 is supported by the executor. |
| `session_time_zone` | `FB_SESSION_TIME_ZONE` | `"UTC"` | Session time zone such as "America/Sao_Paulo" (non-empty str). |
| `client_library` | `FB_CLIENT_LIBRARY` | `None` | Path to a libfbclient to use instead of the bundled one (str \| None). |
| `wire_crypt` | `FB_WIRE_CRYPT` | `"required"` | Wire encryption policy: "required", "enabled" or "disabled"; bools are accepted (True=required, False=disabled). "enabled" allows an unencrypted connection; keep "required" unless the transport is reviewed. |
| `wire_compression` | `FB_WIRE_COMPRESSION` | `False` | Request zlib wire compression; the server must agree. Helps on slow links, costs CPU on fast ones. Check Pool.session_info()["wire_compressed"]. |
| `app_name` | `FB_APP_NAME` | `"fbfast"` | Application name reported to the server (non-empty str). |
| `pool_size` | `FB_POOL_SIZE` | `8` | Maximum connections and native workers (int >= 1); must be >= min_idle. Also the default and maximum concurrency of run_all/run_many. |
| `min_idle` | `FB_MIN_IDLE` | `2` | Connections kept open and ready (0 <= int <= pool_size). Use 0 to keep none. |
| `max_waiters` | `FB_MAX_WAITERS` | `256` | Calls allowed to wait in the queue (int >= 1); a full queue raises PoolBusyError. |
| `acquire_timeout` | `FB_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` | `5.0` | Seconds to obtain a ready connection, including any attach/handshake (float; None not allowed). |
| `connect_timeout` | `FB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | `5.0` | Seconds for attach and handshake, also bounded by acquire_timeout (float). |
| `idle_timeout` | `FB_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | `300.0` | Seconds idle before connections beyond min_idle are closed (float). |
| `max_lifetime` | `FB_MAX_LIFETIME` | `1800.0` | Target connection lifetime in seconds, jittered so recycling spreads out; active work is never interrupted (float). |
| `health_check_after` | `FB_HEALTH_CHECK_AFTER` | `30.0` | Seconds idle after which a connection is pinged; done off the critical path, which also keeps tunnels and NAT mappings alive (float). |
| `close_timeout` | `FB_CLOSE_TIMEOUT` | `10.0` | Seconds to wait for close/cleanup (float). Native work still pending after it stays counted until it finishes. |
| `fetch_size` | `FB_FETCH_SIZE` | `5000` | Target rows per batch (int >= 1); also the default batch_rows of streams. |
| `batch_bytes` | `FB_BATCH_BYTES` | `4_194_304 (4 MiB)` | Byte budget per batch (int >= 1); a single larger row forms its own batch. BLOB batches close once their decoded bytes reach it. Not a limit on total Python memory. |
| `prefetch_batches` | `FB_PREFETCH_BATCHES` | `1` | Batches fetched ahead of the consumer (int >= 0); zero disables read-ahead. |
| `max_result_bytes` | `FB_MAX_RESULT_BYTES` | `536_870_912 (512 MiB)` | Cumulative budget per materialized result (int >= 1 \| None); does not apply to streams and is not an exact RSS cap. None disables it. |
| `max_result_rows` | `FB_MAX_RESULT_ROWS` | `None` | Row limit per materialized result (int >= 1 \| None); does not apply to streams. |
| `max_blob_bytes` | `FB_MAX_BLOB_BYTES` | `67_108_864 (64 MiB)` | Limit per BLOB value, also in streams (int >= 1). Known text charsets count bytes after conversion to UTF-8; exceeding it raises ResultLimitError. |
| `query_timeout` | `FB_QUERY_TIMEOUT` | `30.0` | Default per-query deadline in seconds, including fetching and Python conversion (float \| None). None disables it. |
| `lock_timeout` | `FB_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | `5` | Seconds the server waits for locks (int >= 0); zero means NO WAIT. |
| `stream_idle_timeout` | `FB_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | `30.0` | Seconds a stream producer waits for the consumer to ask for more (float \| None); None disables it. Independent of query_timeout. |
| `statement_cache_size` | `FB_STATEMENT_CACHE_SIZE` | `64` | Prepared statements kept per connection (int >= 0); zero disables the cache. |
| `statement_cache_bytes` | `FB_STATEMENT_CACHE_BYTES` | `8_388_608 (8 MiB)` | Estimated statement cache budget per connection (int >= 1, bytes). |
| `trim_char` | `FB_TRIM_CHAR` | `False` | Strip trailing spaces from CHAR columns, never VARCHAR (bool). |
| `fallback_charset` | `FB_FALLBACK_CHARSET` | `None` | Charset for text without one (charset NONE), str \| None. Currently only UTF8/UTF-8; applies to text and NONE text BLOBs. Invalid bytes raise DataConversionError. |
| `snapshot_timeout` | `FB_SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT` | `300.0` | Deadline for a whole snapshot scope, including time between its queries (float \| None, seconds). Each query inside still uses query_timeout. None disables it. |
| `max_inline_blob_size` | `FB_MAX_INLINE_BLOB_SIZE` | `None` | Largest BLOB a Firebird 5.0.3+ server sends together with its row (int 0..65535 \| None, bytes); 0 disables inline BLOBs. None keeps the client default (65535). |
| `blob_cache_size` | `FB_BLOB_CACHE_SIZE` | `None` | Client cache for inline BLOBs per connection (int >= 0 \| None, bytes). None keeps the client default (10 MiB). |
| `diagnostics` | `FB_DIAGNOSTICS` | `False` | Record time and round trips per phase for every pool query, read with Pool.diagnostics() (bool). Reading the counters adds no round trip. |
| `ready_transaction_timeout` | `FB_READY_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT` | `2.0` | After a query that read all its rows, its session reset also starts the next query's transaction, so the next query skips one round trip; an unused transaction is rolled back after this many idle seconds (float \| None). None disables the reuse. |

`env_file`: path of a dotenv file (str) or `False` to skip it. Omitted: read
`.env` in the current directory if it exists. There is no `FB_ENV_FILE`.
